newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel sees no Framatome-Thomson link.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel sees no Framatome-Thomson link.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk said in an interview on Tuesday that the Thomson and Framatome privatisations were not linked in Alcatel's strategy, and the notion that Alcatel would use Framatome's cash to finance a buyout of Thomson was "absurd".

"The best proof to show that these projects are not linked is that I continue to be interested in Framatome even though the government has expressed its preference for the privatisation of Thomson," he told French newspaper La Tribune. The government said in October it would rather see the electronics company sold to Lagardere Group than to Alcatel.

The government is studying a sale of nuclear reactor manufacturer Framatome to GEC Alsthom, a 50-50 venture between Alcatel and Britain's GEC, under certain conditions. Alcatel is Framatome's biggest shareholder after the government.

Tchuruk said he viewed GEC's demand for an equal share in the venture to Alcatel's "reasonable." "The marriage of French and British management in GEC Alsthom has yielded good results for seven years. I don't see why we'd deprive Framatome of an enlarged version (of that)," he said.
French interests would still dominate in the end, he said, adding that all the positions can be reconciled.
"Simple arithmetic allows us to see that once all the shareholders join around the table, French interests overall will be superior to British interests," he said.
He said there was total agreement "on the subject of continued cooperation with Siemens ".
As for talk that Alcatel might dip into Framatome's cash, Tchuruk said, "You don't pinch the cash of an enterprise."
He said Framatome and GEC Alcatel both had ample cash reserves, ensuring that the merged entity would have the resources to expand internationally.
